paragraphs.text: Lesson 25, an inspiring teacher.
High school students Nate and Ralph are talking about Mr. Smith, their favorite teacher.
Listen to their conversation and answer the comprehension questions.
I thought I was going to flunk chemistry for sure.
Ditto, I just barely squeaked by with a 66 on the final.
The saving grace was that Mr. Smith gave me partial credit for a few of the answers.
Mr. Smith is awesome.
He really cares about his students.
I can't say the same about most of our teachers.
I'm just thanking my lucky stars that I had Mr. Smith for chemistry and not Ms. Johnson.
She's a stickler for perfection.
Or Mr. Potter.
He just drones on without a break.
But Mr. Smith always tries to spice things up with a joke or a game during class.
Let me tell you, when I got my final grades, I breathed a huge sigh of relief.
If I failed that exam, I could have lost my scholarships.
But I didn't, thanks to Mr. Smith.
And I was completely fed up with chemistry and ready to drop the class.
But he went out of his way to help and encourage me.
Did you know that he's 74 years old?
No way, Mr. Smith can't be that old.
He told me he started teaching when he was 29.
And he's been doing it for 45 years, so do the math.
Just think how many students he's helped over the years.
How many lives he's changed?
Yours for one.
If you'd lost your scholarship, you'd probably end up working in your dad's furniture factory.
That's a dead end job.
I don't even want to think about it.
And if I'd failed, I would have gotten an earful from my mom.
Plus we'd both have to make up the credit in summer school.
Hey, why don't we do something nice for Mr. Smith?
You know, to give him props for being such a great teacher?
What do you have in mind?
Well, we can get the gang together and throw a surprise party.
We'll sneak into school early Friday morning and set it up in the classroom.
Sounds cool.
We can also invite the other teachers.
I'm sure they'll have a soft spot for Mr.
Smith.
He's been at this school practically forever.
I can't believe our graduation is just around the corner.
Soon Mr. Smith and everyone else on this place will be a distant memory.
I'll really miss walking into his classroom and listening to him tell his corny jokes.
Are they goofy bow-tay always wears?
Oh man, now I got a lump in my throat.
I wonder if Mr. Smith keeps tabs on his old students, you know, through Facebook or something.
We'll have to look him up.
Yeah, come on.
Let's go play on that party.
Let's learn today's vocabulary.
Ralph says, I thought I was going to flunk chemistry for sure.
The word flunk is a slang word for fail.
Nate replies, ditto.
Ditto means me too.
That's also a slang or informal way to say this.
Nate just barely squeaked by with the 66 on the final.
To squeak by means to barely manage to win, pass or survive something.
But the saving grace for Nate was that Mr. Smith gave him partial credit.
Saving grace means the one thing that makes a situation better or okay.
Ralph likes Mr. Smith because he really cares about his students.
He says, I can't say the same about most of our teachers.
I can't say the same about means in other cases it's different.
In other words, Ralph is saying that most of their teachers don't care about their students.
Nate's thanking his lucky stars that he had Mr. Smith for chemistry and not Ms. Johnson.
To thank your lucky stars means to be extremely grateful for some good fortune.
The other chemistry teacher, Ms. Johnson, is a stickler for perfection.
A stickler is someone who insists on something and is not flexible.
Ralph mentions another teacher, Mr. Potter, who just drones on without a break.
Drone on means to speak continuously in a monotone voice.
But Mr. Smith always tries to spice things up with a joke or game during class.
To spice things up means to make things more interesting, exciting or fun.
When Nate got his final grades, he breathed a huge sigh of relief.
This expression means he was extremely relieved in that moment.
The word sigh means an exhalation of breath like this.
You can sigh when you're frustrated or when you're relieved, as in this case.
Ralph says he was completely fed up with chemistry and ready to drop the class.
If you're fed up with something, that means you're not willing to endure any longer.
You're tired, you're annoyed, and you just want to quit.
But Mr. Smith went out of his way to help and encourage Ralph.
Went out of his way means he made a special effort beyond his normal responsibility.
Ralph is surprised to hear that Mr. Smith is 74 years old.
Nate says Mr. Smith started teaching when he was 29, and he's been doing it for 45 years, so do the math.
Do the math means figure out the answer by yourself.
Mr. Smith's teaching has changed many lives, including Nate's.
Ralph says that if Nate had lost his scholarship, he'd probably end up working in his dad's furniture factory.
Nate describes that as a dead-end job.
A dead-end job is a job with no possibility of advancement, no future.
And if Ralph had failed chemistry, he would have gotten an earful from his mom.
To get an earful from somebody means to have to listen to a lot of criticism or a lot of lecturing.
Plus, Ralph says, we'd both have to make up the credit in summer school.
Makeup the credit means compensate for the academic course needed.
Nate suggests doing something nice for Mr. Smith to give him props for being such a great teacher.
Give him props is an informal way to say express respect and recognition.
Nate's idea is to get the gang together and throw a surprise party.
The word gang in this context is an informal word for a group of friends.
Ralph suggests also inviting the other teachers, because they probably all have a soft spot for Mr. Smith.
To have a soft spot for someone means to have a bit of special affection for that person.
Nate can't believe that their graduation is just around the corner.
Just around the corner, in this context, means very soon in the future.
Ralph says he'll miss walking into Mr. Smith's classroom and listening to him tell his corny jokes.
If something is corny, it means it is ridiculous and a bit exaggerated, not very sophisticated or elegant.
And Nate talks about the goofy bow tie that Mr. Smith always wears.
Goofy means silly.
Then Nate says, aww man, now I've got a lump in my throat.
If you've got a lump in your throat, it means your feeling like your throat is tight, as if you are going to cry due to strong emotion.
Ralph wonders if Mr. Smith keeps tabs on his old students, like through Facebook.
To keep tabs on someone or something means to observe over time.
Ralph and Nate end the conversation by deciding to go plan the party.
That's all the vocabulary from today's conversation.
